UX surfaceBoot surfaces: what the user sees first on each bundle.

Members

Skeleton

Public wasm surface — one skeleton canvas per instance. A page may mount several (hero + content areas shimmer independently).

frame

frame — one animation tick. Per-frame cost: one ~64 B uniform write + one pass + one 3-vertex draw. The fragment loop early- outs per rect — bounded and cheap.

  • @param dt Seconds since the previous frame call.
  • @param {number} dt

init

init — acquire adapter/device, configure the canvas, compile the pipeline, allocate the uniform + sheet buffers. Rejection propagates to JS, which falls back to the WebGL/CSS skeleton.

  • @param canvas The dedicated canvas this surface paints.
  • @param device The shared GPUDevice (one per page, from the JS bridge).
  • @returns Ok on a configured surface, Err(JsValue) on failure.
  • @param {HTMLCanvasElement} canvas
  • @param {GPUDevice} device

constructor

Skeleton::new — un-initialized surface; init must follow. Split because the device request is an async browser promise.

resize

resize — re-configure the surface after a canvas-bitmap change + store the DEVICE-pixel size as the shader's rect (the whole-canvas clip, in frag's device units).

  • @param w Device-pixel width (element CSS px × DPR).
  • @param h Device-pixel height.
  • @param {number} w
  • @param {number} h

set_size

set_size — the canvas's CSS-pixel size. Feeds the shader's res field (the widget rect IS the whole canvas — device-px rect is written by resize instead).

  • @param w Canvas width in CSS pixels.
  • @param h Canvas height in CSS pixels.
  • @param {number} w
  • @param {number} h

set_state

set_state — scalar updates bundled to keep the JS call count low: resolve progress, ink alpha, live rect count.

  • @param resolve 0..1 resolve progress (collapse+fade driver).
  • @param ink_alpha Global glyph opacity multiplier.
  • @param count Live rect count, clamped to MAX_RECTS.
  • @param {number} resolve
  • @param {number} ink_alpha
  • @param {number} count

write_sheet

write_sheet — upload the per-rect data block: 16 f32s per rect — [x,y,w,h][radius,cell,row_h,unused][sbase rgb,unused] [sink rgb,unused]. Truncated at MAX_RECTS rows; count (set via set_state) decides how many rows the GPU reads.

  • @param values Flat f32 sheet — 16 values per rect row.
  • @param {Float32Array} values
